name: Martin Bormann
role: Head of the Nazi Party Chancellery (1941-45) and Hitler's private secretary (1943-45); died 1945
summary: Martin Bormann, head of the Nazi Party Chancellery and Hitler's secretary, ran the Party apparatus, signed decrees extending the Nuremberg Laws and placing Jews under the Gestapo, organised forced resettlement and slave-labour policies, and led the most hostile anti-Christian line inside the leadership.

sources.title: Judgment of the International Military Tribunal: Bormann, 30 September 1946, The Avalon Project (Yale)
sources.author: International Military Tribunal, Nuremberg
sources.usedFor: The Tribunal's findings of what he signed and ordered: the 31 May 1941 extension of the Nuremberg Laws, the 12 August 1942 order on forced resettlement and denationalisation, the 9 October 1942 and 1 July 1943 orders on Jews, slave labour, prisoners of war.

sources.title: Circular Letter Nr. 72/38 (17 June 1938) by Bormann forbidding religious practice and participation in religious celebrations in the Reich Labour Service (Nuremberg document PS-107), Harvard Law School Nuremberg Trials Project
sources.author: Martin Bormann (Staff Leader of the Deputy of the Fuehrer)
sources.usedFor: His circular passing on the order that every religious practice is forbidden in the Reich Labour Service.

sources.title: Circular of 3 June 1939 (PS-838) enforcing the ban on Party members belonging to Christian Science, Harvard Law School Nuremberg Trials Project
sources.author: Martin Bormann
sources.usedFor: His enforcement of the decree barring Christian Science adherents from the Party.

sources.title: Martin Bormann's Confidential Memo: National Socialism and Christianity are Irreconcilable (6 June 1941), German History in Documents and Images (translation from Nazi Conspiracy and Aggression, vol. VI)
sources.author: Martin Bormann
sources.usedFor: His secret circular: Christianity rests on dogma and uncertainty, National Socialism on science, and the churches' influence must be ended.

sources.title: Letter from Bormann to Alfred Rosenberg, 22 February 1940 (PS-098), on directions for religious instruction in schools, Harvard Law School Nuremberg Trials Project
sources.author: Martin Bormann
sources.usedFor: His view that Christian teaching and National Socialism are incompatible and that school religious instruction must be replaced by a National Socialist 'life formulation'.

sources.title: The Bormann Letters: the private correspondence between Martin Bormann and his wife Gerda, July 1943 to April 1945, ed. H. R. Trevor-Roper (1954), Internet Archive full text
sources.author: Martin Bormann (his letters to Gerda Bormann; her letters were not counted)
sources.usedFor: His own private words on Jewry, Christianity and Hitler.

notes: First audit. Acts rest on the Nuremberg Tribunal's judgment on Bormann (findings of what he signed and ordered, from documents bearing his signature) and two circulars he issued; his words are the June 1941 confidential memo, the 1940 letter to Rosenberg and his own letters to his wife in The Bormann Letters (Gerda Bormann's letters and the editor's commentary were not counted as his). Hitler's Table Talk, which Bormann's office recorded, is Hitler's speech and was not used. Answers keep the two kinds apart. Searched without a settled answer: slave labour and prisoner-of-war orders (no matching statement beyond population-transfer), his ordering that no action be taken against lynchers of Allied airmen (no matching statement), nationalism and expansion (the judgment finds no proof he knew of Hitler's aggressive-war plans before 1941), the economy, the family and women. Other statements stay null. The Nazi Party's and Hitler's positions were not attributed to him.
